To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
solar fractions of 70% for space heating and 50% for domestic hot water supply can be achieved with a solar thermal system using a PCM heat storage based on stable supercooling.
the solar fraction of domestic hot water can be increased by 20% with the presented PCM storage concept.
the solar thermal combisystems with stable supercooled PCM heat storage are feasible for space heating and DHW supply of single family buildings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel PCM based solar heat storage concept, which allows for high solar fractions and a low storage volume.
the simulation and optimization of the novel solar thermal storage concept for space heating and hot water supply of buildings.
the development of a novel PCM storage concept for long term heat supply.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solar fraction of space heating and domestic water supply is strongly depending on the collector area.
the concept of stable PCM supercooling is feasible and can be applied to a solar thermal combi system.
the solar share on the domestic hot water supply is strongly depending on the building characteristics and the domestic hot water demand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stable supercooling is an attractive method for seasonal heat storage in solar thermal combisystems.
the presented system concept is suitable for the application in single family houses and that solar fractions of up to 80% for space heating and 50% for hot water supply can be achieved.
the concept of stable Supercooling of Sodium acetate trihydrate (SAT) has the potential to increase solar fraction of heat supply of single-family houses.

the presented concept of stable supercooled PCM is a promising technology to increase solar fractions in heat energy supply of buildings.
the concept of stable PCM supercooling is suitable for seasonal heat storage in solar thermal systems.
